title: Agreed Until It Mattered, Explained
subtitle: Casimir Beng, Osei Vandermeer and Renke Sabel on a cheap sensor rig, a bowling alley's own scoring system, and whose calls the league's rules committee believes
summary: A research explainer from the School of Continuous Improvement on Casimir Beng, Osei Vandermeer and Renke Sabel's season-long audit of a cheap sensor rig against a ten-pin bowling alley's own scoring and foul-detection system. It follows the season's disputed frames from the two systems' calls to an independent slow-motion video review, and on to the league's rules committee. Beng, Sabel and Vandermeer describe the work in their own words.
topic: A research explainer of the paper auditing a cheap sensor comparator rig against a ten-pin bowling alley's proprietary lane-scoring and foul-detection system across a league season, and whose calls on disputed frames the league's rules committee upholds

beats.text: The process tracks which system was already installed, not which was more often right.
A comparator only tells you two systems disagree. It doesn’t tell a committee which one to believe, and ours evidently didn’t change that.
